rows.micah_quote: Friston's framework posits that the brain is constantly making predictions about sensory input and attempting to minimize the difference between its predictions and actual sensory data, which is what he calls "active inference." This mechanism of prediction helps maintain an internal model of the world, contributing to how we experience perception, cognition, and action.
